description: Indulge in the rich, creamy flavors of homemade Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani), a beloved Indian classic. This iconic dish features tender chicken pieces simmered in a velvety tomato-based sauce, enriched with butter, cream, and aromatic spices. It's the perfect comforting meal for any occasion, especially a satisfying Indian lunch.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons butter. Once melted, add the cinnamon stick, green cardamom pods, and cloves. Saute for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Mixture
instructions.text: Add the pureed tomatoes, remaining 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt to the pan. Bring to a simmer, then add the soaked cashews. Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate.

instructions.title: Blend and Finish the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the whole spices (cinnamon, cardamom, cloves) if desired. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for a super silky texture. Return the pan to low heat.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Sauce
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces, remaining 1 tablespoon butter, sugar, and heavy cream to the smooth sauce. Stir well to combine. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to heat through. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms and stir it into the butter chicken.

instructions.title: Serve Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the chicken slightly on a grill or under a broiler before adding it to the sauce.
Do not skip blending the sauce and passing it through a sieve; this is key to achieving the signature silky smooth texture of authentic Murgh Makhani.
If you don't have cashews, you can substitute with blanched almonds for a similar richness and thickening effect.
article:
Mastering the Art of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Indian Lunch Guide

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's known in Hindi, is more than just a dish; it's a culinary hug in a bowl. This iconic Indian lunch recipe has captivated palates worldwide with its rich, creamy tomato gravy and tender pieces of chicken. Originating in the bustling kitchens of Delhi, it has evolved into a global favorite, synonymous with comforting Indian cuisine. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore new flavors, preparing authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a rewarding experience that promises a burst of flavor in every bite.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani translates literally to "chicken with butter," and true to its name, butter is a star ingredient, contributing to its luxurious texture and taste. This dish is characterized by succulent pieces of chicken, traditionally marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried until tender. The real magic, however, lies in its velvety smooth sauce. This gravy is a harmonious blend of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, green chilies, and a delicate balance of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and coriander. A generous dollop of butter and a swirl of cream are added at the end, giving the sauce its signature richness and a slightly sweet, tangy profile that sets it apart from other curries. It’s a milder curry, making it incredibly appealing to a wide audience, including those who prefer less heat but still crave complex flavors. It’s a quintessential Indian lunch recipe, often enjoyed with naan bread or basmati rice.

## Ingredients You Need

To create your own unforgettable Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani, gather these essential ingredients:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Makhani (Butter) Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   2 green chilies, slit (adjust to your spice preference)
*   800g canned crushed tomatoes or 6-7 ripe fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup cashew nuts, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes
*   1/2 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1/2 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances tomato acidity)
*   1/2 cup water (or chicken broth)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or cashew paste for dairy-free)
*   1 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh coriander leaves for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches and cook until nicely browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with 1 tablespoon of oil. Add the chopped onion and sauté until golden brown and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
4.  **Aromatics and Spices:** Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to bloom the spices.
5.  **Tomatoes and Cashews:** Pour in the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree) and the soaked, blended cashew paste. Add sugar, salt, and 1/2 cup of water. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.
6.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
7.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low heat. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces. Add the garam masala and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the sauce.
8.  **The Creamy Finish:** Finally, stir in the heavy cream. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, just until heated through. Do not boil after adding cream. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse deep flavor, essential for a truly delicious Butter Chicken.
*   **Good Quality Tomatoes:** Use ripe, flavorful fresh tomatoes or high-quality canned crushed tomatoes. They form the backbone of the sauce, so their taste profoundly impacts the final dish.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** For that restaurant-quality texture, ensure your sauce is blended until absolutely smooth. Straining it afterwards is an extra step that makes a noticeable difference.
*   **Balance Sweetness and Acidity:** Tomatoes can be quite acidic. A touch of sugar helps balance this and enhances the overall flavor profile of the Murgh Makhani.
*   **Kasoori Methi Magic:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are non-negotiable for authentic Butter Chicken. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils.
*   **Don't Overcook the Cream:** Add the cream at the very end and just heat it through. Boiling the sauce after adding cream can sometimes cause it to split or lose its velvety texture.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a showstopper on its own, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments.
*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps soak up the delicious gravy.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita (yogurt dip) can offer a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.
*   **Salad:** A simple side salad with thinly sliced red onions and a squeeze of lemon can add a fresh crunch.
This makes for a fantastic and fulfilling Indian lunch.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is perfect as is, you can adapt it to suit different dietary needs or preferences.
*   **Vegetarian Butter Paneer:** Replace chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese), mushrooms, or mixed vegetables. Marinate paneer lightly in spices before adding to the sauce.
*   **Dairy-Free:** Use coconut cream instead of heavy cream and a plant-based butter alternative. For the marinade, use a dairy-free yogurt. Cashew paste already helps with thickness, making it easier to skip dairy.
*   **Spicier Version:** Increase the number of green chilies or add a pinch more red chili powder to the sauce. You can also add a finely chopped red chili as a garnish.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you have a grill, lightly grill the marinated chicken until it develops a slight char before adding it to the sauce for an authentic smoky touch.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or use a low-fat cream alternative. The cashew paste still provides richness without excessive fat.

Creating your own Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani at home is a culinary journey that rewards you with incredible flavors and the satisfaction of mastering a beloved Indian classic. This rich, creamy, and utterly delicious dish is perfect for a special Indian lunch or a comforting dinner, promising to delight anyone who tastes it. So, roll up your sleeves, gather your ingredients, and prepare to create a masterpiece that will have everyone asking for seconds!
